text.content: When basic RAG is not enough

rich_text.plain_text: When basic RAG is not enough

text.content:
Contigo GmbH's development team has a working understanding of the RAG pipeline. Documents are ingested, chunked, embedded, and stored. At query time, the client's question is converted into a vector, the closest matching chunks are retrieved, and the language model generates a grounded response.
For a single isolated question, this works well. But Contigo's support agent is not handling isolated questions. It is handling conversations which are multi-turn exchanges where each question builds on what came before.

text.content: Consider this exchange:

rich_text.plain_text: Consider this exchange:

text.content: Turn 1 Client:

rich_text.plain_text: Turn 1 Client:

text.content: "What are the eligibility criteria for the SME Standard loan?"

rich_text.plain_text: "What are the eligibility criteria for the SME Standard loan?"

text.content: Turn 2 Client:

rich_text.plain_text: Turn 2 Client:

text.content: "And what about the repayment conditions for that one?”

rich_text.plain_text: "And what about the repayment conditions for that one?”

text.content: In a basic RAG system, Turn 2 is sent to the vector database exactly as written: "And what about the repayment conditions for that one?" The phrase "that one" has no meaning outside the context of Turn 1. The vector database has no knowledge of the previous exchange. It searches for chunks semantically similar to "repayment conditions for that one" and returns either nothing useful or a chunk from the wrong product section. The agent fails not because the information is missing from the knowledge base, but because the retrieval system had no way to know what "that one" referred to.

text.content: How to improve conversational retrieval in n8n

rich_text.plain_text: How to improve conversational retrieval in n8n

text.content: In n8n, build an explicit two-step process: an LLM rewrites the context-dependent query using recent chat history, then the retriever searches Qdrant with the standalone question. This reformulation is not automatic in the vector-store node.

text.content: Step 1: Query reformulation -

rich_text.plain_text: Step 1: Query reformulation -

text.content: Before the query reaches the vector database, a Basic LLM Chain uses the current question and relevant history from your n8n memory setup. The language model rewrites the query into a standalone question that can be understood without the surrounding conversation.

text.content: Top K

rich_text.plain_text: Top K

text.content: — The number of chunks retrieved per query. A higher value gives the language model more context but risks diluting the signal with loosely related chunks. A lower value keeps the context focused but risks missing relevant information.

rich_text.plain_text: — The number of chunks retrieved per query. A higher value gives the language model more context but risks diluting the signal with loosely related chunks. A lower value keeps the context focused but risks missing relevant information.

text.content: System prompt grounding

rich_text.plain_text: System prompt grounding

text.content: — The instruction that tells the language model how strictly to use the retrieved chunks. A weak instruction allows the model to supplement with its training data. A strong prohibition prevents it.

rich_text.plain_text: — The instruction that tells the language model how strictly to use the retrieved chunks. A weak instruction allows the model to supplement with its training data. A strong prohibition prevents it.

text.content: Chunk quality

rich_text.plain_text: Chunk quality

text.content: — Determined by the chunking and preparation decisions made. The Qdrant retriever returns the chunks indexed into the selected collection. If the chunks are poorly prepared, query reformulation cannot compensate for them.

text.content: Embedding model consistency

rich_text.plain_text: Embedding model consistency

text.content: — The same embedding model must be used during ingestion and at query time. A mismatch produces meaningless similarity scores regardless of how well the query is reformulated.

text.content: What is beyond the scope of this workflow

rich_text.plain_text: What is beyond the scope of this workflow

text.content: The proposed n8n workflow follows a fixed sequence: rewrite the query, retrieve relevant chunks once, and generate an answer. It does not evaluate whether the retrieved chunks are sufficient, re-query if they are not, or route queries to different knowledge bases based on their content.

text.content: These capabilities belong to a more advanced architecture called agentic RAG. Agentic RAG introduces an autonomous reasoning layer into the retrieval process itself, allowing the system to plan, evaluate, and iterate before generating a response. This is beyond the scope of the current n8n exercise but represents the direction the industry is moving for complex, multi-source retrieval tasks.

text.content: Takeaway:

rich_text.plain_text: Takeaway:

text.content: Query reformulation improves on basic RAG by reformulating ambiguous follow-up queries into standalone questions before retrieval begins. This makes multi-turn conversations reliable in a way that single-shot RAG cannot be.
